content:
From: Sara Turner <sara.turner@aurelia-health.com>

Subject: Tokens-per-USD sanity check for MAP pilot & close timeline

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. We want to finalize the MAP and lock an evaluation window, but before legal and procurement get comfortable we need a short, quantified sanity check of the unit economics you put in the MAP spreadsheet. Two concrete asks:

1) Can you confirm the tokens-per-USD numbers you're using for the recommended model variants (hosted Redwood-3 and the quantized dedicated variant)? We need the per-token cost breakdown and any licensing/overhead assumptions.

2) We want to validate caching and batching assumptions in the eval. What hit rates and batching factors should we expect in a first-pass pilot for our 15K daily active users traffic profile? If you can provide a short note and a timeline (how long for an eval that gives statistically meaningful cost numbers), procurement can sketch the PO.

Attachments: MAP_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (the file you shared)

Goal: close by end of June if we can validate economics quickly.

Cheers,
Sara
Sara Turner
Head of Product, Aurelia Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Turner <sara.turner@aurelia-health.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Tokens-per-USD sanity check for MAP pilot & close timeline

Sara — thanks, quick response below and attached a lightly annotated workbook (MAP_unit_econ_v1.xlsx). I kept this tight so procurement can ingest it quickly.

Summary (short):
- Recommended models: hosted "redwood-3.7B" (default for latency-sensitive flows) and "redwood-3-q4" (quantized, dedicated pool) as the fallback to reduce $/token for heavy volume.
- Per-token basis (hosted list price estimates used in MAP):
  • redwood-3.7B (hosted): ~$0.000016 / token (includes infra & infra margin)
  • redwood-3-q4 (dedicated, amortized infra + reserved capacity): ~$0.000010 / token (assumes committed capacity, see workbook)
- Overheads considered: network egress (~0.5%), request orchestration / rate-limiter amortization (~1%), and monitoring/retention add-on (optional). I rolled them into the per-token values above.

Key MAP assumptions (what to validate in eval):
- Avg tokens per user request (front-end prompt + assistant): 420 tokens (median 180, tail 1k+ for long sessions).
- Session composition: 3 requests / session on average -> tokens/session ~ 1,260.
- Caching (prefix/KV) assumptions: first-request cache miss rate 0%; subsequent requests within a session estimated hit rate 60% for repeated contexts (forms, templates). Overall effective token reduction from caching: ~18% on baseline traffic.
- Batching factor: we assume a conservative batching factor of 1.7x on average (peaks lower due to latency SLOs). That yields ~15% token-cost reduction vs no-batching when applied.
- Combined effective tokens-per-dollar estimate (hosted): with the numbers above, expected tokens per USD ~ 62.5k tokens / $1 (hosted redwood-3.7B). For dedicated/quantized fallback, tokens per USD rises to ~100k tokens / $1.

Operational notes and risks:
- If the real session length or user concurrency differs (e.g., many short single-turn requests), caching benefit will be lower and tokens/$ will drop.
- Prefetching templates can increase token usage; avoid until after pilot confirms net UX lift.
- For procurement, recommend a small committed starter on Dedicated (4–8 GPUs equivalent) to realize the better tokens/$ on steady-state traffic.

Pilot & timeline suggestion:
- Quick validation: 7-day live pilot with a 2% traffic shadow of production (random sampling) should yield a cost signal within ±10% if we capture representative concurrency.
- Minimal instrumentation: log per-request tokens, cache hit tags, batch sizes. I included the fields in the workbook.
- Deliverable: annotated MAP workbook + short readout (1 pager) after 7 days. If both sides agree, finalize PO & rollout by June 27.

Attachment: MAP_unit_econ_v1.xlsx (annotated)

Let me know if you want the numbers broken down differently or want a worked example with your traffic profile (I can sketch with your daily active user numbers).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Tokens-per-USD sanity check for MAP pilot & close timeline

Jonas / team — reviewed and small adjustments below. I also attached a CSV with the row-level calcs (calc_numbers.csv) to make it easy for procurement to import.

Corrections / clarifications:
- Per-token numbers: I agree with the hosted baseline but suggest we be explicit about what "token" pricing includes. The hosted figure Jonas used (~$0.000016/token) assumes 8k context, no extra retention, and the standard support bundle. If Aurelia needs higher retention logs or HIPAA add-on, add ~8% to hosted cost; call that out in the MAP.
- Caching: 60% within-session hit-rate is optimistic for the first-week pilot. Recommend we model two scenarios in the workbook: conservative (40% hit on repeat requests) and optimistic (60%); use conservative for procurement.
- Batching: the 1.7x batching factor was reasonable, but for latency-sensitive healthcare flows we'll plan for 1.4x during the pilot (optimize for UX over cost). That drops the batching savings from ~15% to ~10%.

Updated combined tokens-per-USD (conservative pilot assumptions):
- Hosted redwood-3.7B: ~52k tokens / $1 (conservative caching 40% + batching 1.4x)
- Dedicated quantized: ~85k tokens / $1 (assumes committed capacity + q4 accuracy trade-offs)

Pilot design recommendation (actionable):
1) 7-day window, 3% traffic shadowing (random sample of real users) — should surface caching behaviour and average tokens per session.
2) Instrumentation: per-request token count, cache-hit flag, batch-id tag, model-variant label. We can supply a patch to the SDK to add the flags in 24 hours.
3) Measure: tokens/day, cost/day, cache-hit %, mean batch size, 95th pct latency.
4) Decision gates: if tokens/day cost deviates more than 15% from workbook baseline after day 5, pause expansion and run deep dive.

Timeline: if SDK patch + instrumentation go in by Monday (6/16), we can run 7-day pilot 6/17–6/23 and deliver a readout 6/24. Procurement/PO can then be finalized and signed by 6/27.

I'll update the workbook with conservative numbers and send back.

—Karthik
